narrative.overview: A frightened reader gets the sign system of a metro at night: near-black panels, enamel lettering, ten lettered lines, stations, a green exit. Flat, tonal, square-cornered; nothing moves unless the reader tapped.
keyCharacteristics: Night default with a full day theme
Ten line colours in two values, always with a letter
Amber for danger only, exit green for leaving only
Overpass 800 signs over Atkinson Next reading
Circle = line/station, rectangle = sign/control, triangle = safety
No shadows; five tap-caused motions, transform/opacity only

rules.name: The Letter Rule
rules.body: A line colour is never used without its letter or name beside it.

rules.name: The Danger-Only Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means safety only; never emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Exit-Only Green Rule
rules.body: Green means leave; never success or saved.

rules.name: The Two-Values Rule
rules.body: Every line colour has a night and a day value.

rules.name: The Sign-vs-Read Rule
rules.body: Scanned text is Overpass 800; read text is Atkinson.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate by tone, rule, or inset ring; never blur or offset shadows.

rules.name: The Shape-Means Rule
rules.body: Circle = line/station, rectangle = sign/control, triangle = safety.

dos: Do put one white primary blade or button per screen.
Do pair every line colour with its letter.
Do keep Leave in the top bar in exit green.
Do gate new motion behind reduced-motion and animate transform/opacity only.
Do run scripts/decoder-verify.js after any change.
donts: Don't use amber except for safety or green except for leaving.
Don't use colour alone to separate lines or states.
Don't round buttons or square the circles of lines.
Don't add drop shadows or unprompted motion.
